title: Anatomy of a Scam Call: What 10,000 real scam and spam calls reveal about how phone scammers operate
abstract: arXiv:2608.24127v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Telephone fraud is pervasive and costly, but its inner workings are rarely observed at scale. We analyze a complete corpus of 10,211 inbound scam and spam calls -- 913 hours of audio and 330,956 transcribed turns from 5,780 distinct numbers -- collected over 54 days by an AI voice-agent honeypot that answered callers and kept them talking, and introduced in a companion data descriptor. We separate outright scams, which solicit sensitive information, from the larger stream of predatory but legal lead generation ("spam") that feeds them. Scam operations keep office hours (6.6x more calls per weekday than weekend day); thousands of disposable numbers run a small catalog of recycled scripts (thirty opening clusters, half the traffic in the top five); and callers solicit identity anchors -- a home address and a date of birth -- far more often than payment credentials, pressing through persistence and manufactured authority rather than overt

translated_title: 诈骗电话剖析：10,000个真实诈骗和垃圾电话揭示电话诈骗者的运作方式
translated_abstract: 电话欺诈普遍存在且代价高昂，但其内部运作方式很少在大规模范围内被观察到。我们分析了一个包含10,211个入站诈骗和垃圾电话的完整语料库——包括913小时的音频和来自5,780个不同号码的330,956个转录轮次——这些数据是通过一个AI语音代理蜜罐在54天内收集的，该蜜罐接听来电者并让他们持续交谈，并在配套数据描述中进行了介绍。我们将直接索取敏感信息的绝对诈骗，与更大规模的掠夺性但合法的线索生成（“垃圾电话”）区分开来，后者为前者提供养分。诈骗活动保持办公时间（工作日的电话量是周末的6.6倍）；数千个一次性号码运行着少量循环使用的脚本（三十个开场群组，前五名占据了一半流量）；来电者索取身份锚点——家庭住址和出生日期——的频率远高于支付凭证，通过坚持和制造权威而非公开强迫来施压。
tldr: 本研究通过分析10,000多个真实诈骗和垃圾电话，揭示了电话诈骗者通常在工作时间运营、使用有限脚本，并优先索取身份信息而非支付凭证的运作模式。
en_tdlr: This study analyzes over 10,000 real scam and spam calls to reveal that phone scammers typically operate during business hours, use a limited set of scripts, and prioritize soliciting identity information over payment credentials.
